plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 12: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic strip of the electromagnetic spectrum covering the infrared region and its neighbors. A horizontal band, with ragged torn edges at both ends to signal that the spectrum continues past the drawing, is divided into six colored segments labeled left to right "Ultraviolet" in deep purple, a narrow "Visible" in medium violet, "Near infrared" in pale pink, a wide "Infrared" in stronger pink, "Far infrared" in very pale pink, and "Microwaves" in pale green. Beneath it runs a wavelength scale marked "lambda (cm)" with labeled decade ticks at 10^-5, 10^-4, 10^-3, 10^-2, and 10^-1. Two thin leader lines rise from annotations below to the inner boundaries of the "Infrared" segment: the left reads lambda = 2.5 x 10^-4 cm, = 2.5 micrometers, wavenumber 4000 cm^-1; the right reads lambda = 2.5 x 10^-3 cm, = 25 micrometers, wavenumber 400 cm^-1. Above the band a broad arrow shaded from pale yellow at its tail to deep orange-red at its head points leftward and is labeled "Energy", set opposite the wavelength scale so the two read as inverse across the same width. The span between the leader lines picks out the narrow midportion of the infrared that organic chemists actually use.

interactionPlan.concept: Wavelength, wavenumber, and photon energy are inverse expressions of the same quantity, and the infrared region chemists actually use for structure determination is the narrow 2.5–25 µm (4000–400 cm⁻¹) window.
elements: Horizontal spectrum band with ragged torn left and right edges indicating the spectrum continues
Segment: Ultraviolet (deep purple), leftmost, ending near 2.5×10⁻⁵ cm
Segment: Visible (medium violet), narrow
Segment: Near infrared (pale pink), ending at 2.5×10⁻⁴ cm
Segment: Infrared (stronger pink), spanning 2.5×10⁻⁴ to 2.5×10⁻³ cm
Segment: Far infrared (very pale pink)
Segment: Microwaves (pale green), rightmost
Logarithmic wavelength axis beneath the band labeled 'λ (cm)' with decade ticks at 10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁴, 10⁻³, 10⁻², 10⁻¹
Left leader line from the 2.5×10⁻⁴ cm boundary down to annotation: 'λ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ cm, = 2.5 µm, ṽ = 4000 cm⁻¹'
Right leader line from the 2.5×10⁻³ cm boundary down to annotation: 'λ = 2.5 × 10⁻³ cm, = 25 µm, ṽ = 400 cm⁻¹'
Broad leftward-pointing arrow above the band, gradient pale yellow (tail, right) to deep orange-red (head, left), labeled 'Energy'
Draggable vertical marker line crossing the band with a handle on the wavelength axis
Readout panel showing current λ in cm, λ in µm, wavenumber ṽ in cm⁻¹, photon energy in kJ/mol, and the name of the region under the marker

interactions.label: Wavelength λ (log₁₀ of cm)
interactions.teaches: Sliding toward longer wavelength moves the marker right while wavenumber and photon energy fall together — the three scales are inverses of one another, not independent axes.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The 4000–400 cm⁻¹ band used in organic structure determination is only a sliver of the whole electromagnetic spectrum, and only the middle of the infrared itself.
Each named region corresponds to a definite wavelength span and a definite kind of molecular excitation (electronic, vibrational, rotational).

demo_steps.title: The spectrum strip
demo_steps.narration: A single logarithmic wavelength axis runs from ultraviolet on the left to microwaves on the right. Hover any colored region to see its wavelength span and what kind of molecular motion it excites.

demo_steps.title: Short wavelength, high energy
demo_steps.narration: Drag the marker into the ultraviolet: λ is small, the wavenumber is huge, and the energy readout is large — matching the deep red head of the Energy arrow pointing left.

demo_steps.title: Long wavelength, low energy
demo_steps.narration: Now drag to the microwave end. Wavelength has grown a thousandfold and both wavenumber and energy have dropped by the same factor — the Energy arrow fades to pale yellow here.

demo_steps.title: The 4000 cm⁻¹ edge
demo_steps.narration: Park the marker on the left leader line: λ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ cm = 2.5 µm = 4000 cm⁻¹. This is the high-energy boundary of the region an IR spectrometer scans.

demo_steps.title: The 400 cm⁻¹ edge
demo_steps.narration: Slide to the right leader line: λ = 2.5 × 10⁻³ cm = 25 µm = 400 cm⁻¹. Ten times the wavelength, one tenth the wavenumber and energy.

demo_steps.title: Zoom to the working window
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the organic IR window: the figure expands the 2.5–25 µm span and relabels the axis in wavenumbers from 4000 down to 400 cm⁻¹, the scale every IR spectrum is plotted on.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Wavelength, wavenumber, and energy are one variable seen three ways — and the whole of IR structure determination happens inside one narrow decade of it, 4000 to 400 cm⁻¹.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Build as a wide SVG. Center: a horizontal band of six abutting colored rectangles with thin dark dividers and torn/wavy vertical edges at far left and far right; color order left→right deep purple (Ultraviolet), medium violet (Visible, narrow), pale pink (Near infrared), saturated pink (Infrared, widest), very pale pink (Far infrared), pale sage green (Microwaves), each with its name centered in dark text. Directly below, a log wavelength axis labeled 'λ (cm)' at far left with decade ticks 10⁻⁵ … 10⁻¹ evenly spaced; segment boundaries must land at their correct log positions (IR spans 2.5×10⁻⁴ to 2.5×10⁻³ cm). Two thin elbowed leader lines drop from those two IR boundaries to annotation blocks below reading λ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ cm / = 2.5 µm / ṽ = 4000 cm⁻¹ and λ = 2.5 × 10⁻³ cm / = 25 µm / ṽ = 400 cm⁻¹. Above the band a thick leftward arrow with a horizontal gradient from pale yellow at the right tail to deep orange-red at the left head, bold 'Energy' label centered on it. Overlay a draggable vertical marker line (dark, with a round handle on the axis) plus a readout card near the top-right showing λ (cm), λ (µm), ṽ (cm⁻¹), E (kJ/mol) and the current region name, values recomputed live. In the 'Organic IR window' view, dim everything outside the IR segment, stretch the 2.5–25 µm span across the full width, and swap the bottom axis to a decreasing wavenumber scale (4000, 3000, 2000, 1500, 1000, 400 cm⁻¹) to mirror how IR spectra are conventionally plotted.

authoredContext:
In infrared (IR) spectroscopy, the IR region of the electromagnetic spectrum covers the range from just above the visible (7.8 × 10–7 m) to approximately 10–4 m, but only the midportion from 2.5 × 10–6 m to 2.5 × 10–5 m is used by organic chemists (the figure. Wavelengths within the IR region are usually given in micrometers (1 μm = 10–6 m), and frequencies are given in wavenumbers rather than in hertz. The wavenumber v˜ is the reciprocal of wavelength in centimeters and is therefore expressed in units of cm–1.

Thus, the useful IR region is from 4000 to 400 cm–1, corresponding to energies of 48.0 kJ/mol to 4.80 kJ/mol (11.5–1.15 kcal/mol).

The infrared and adjacent regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

A partial electromagnetic spectrum extending from ultraviolet through visible light and infrared to microwave radiation, where ultraviolet is higher in energy and microwave is lower.

Why does an organic molecule absorb some wavelengths of IR radiation but not others? All molecules have a certain amount of energy and are in constant motion. Their bonds stretch and contract, atoms wag back and forth, and other molecular vibrations occur. Some of the kinds of allowed vibrations are shown below:

attempts.html:
Guided demo

1 / 6 Drag the round handle on the axis, or hover / click a coloured region.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: All text in the SVG is rendered at ~55% scale (1100-unit viewBox in a ~600 px pane), so region labels (~9 px), the λ callout blocks (~9 px) and especially the 'Marker readout' card (~7 px) are noticeably smaller and harder to read than the bold, comfortably-sized type in the source.

The default state adds elements absent from the source: a black vertical marker line with a round handle cutting through the Infrared band, and an opaque 'Marker readout' box sitting below the Far-infrared/Microwaves region — extra chrome that changes the at-a-glance look of the strip.

The Energy arrow is proportionally thinner/shorter relative to the band than in the source (source arrow bar is nearly as tall as a third of the strip with a much larger arrowhead), and the bold 'Energy' word is far smaller relative to the figure.

'Near infrared' is rendered as two lines in different sizes/colours (second line smaller and grey) whereas the source uses identical type for both lines; other region labels are also lighter weight than the source.
The torn/wavy edges at the far left and far right are much smaller in amplitude than the pronounced scalloped edges in the source, weakening the 'spectrum continues' cue.
Vertical whitespace: the figure occupies only the upper ~70% of the pane with a large empty area beneath, unlike the tightly cropped source.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful recreation of the IR spectrum strip with correct region order, colours, gradient Energy arrow and both λ/ν̃ callouts, backed by genuinely useful interactions (draggable marker, wavenumber readout, zoom-to-IR-window toggle, 6-step demo), but the whole SVG is down-scaled so nearly all text — particularly the readout card — is uncomfortably small, and default-state marker/readout chrome adds elements not in the source.

feedback.rationale: The concept, region structure, and interaction set are correct; the remaining issues are implementation-level (text scale/viewBox, default marker/readout chrome, arrow proportions, torn-edge amplitude, vertical cropping) that the generator can fix directly.

demo_steps.narration: Slide to the right leader line: λ = 2.5 × 10⁻³ cm = 25 µm = 400 cm⁻¹. Ten times the wavelength, one tenth the wavenumber and energy.

demo_steps.title: Zoom to the working window
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the organic IR window: the figure expands the 2.5–25 µm span and relabels the axis in wavenumbers from 4000 down to 400 cm⁻¹, the scale every IR spectrum is plotted on.

plan.keyInsight: Wavelength, wavenumber, and energy are one variable seen three ways — and the whole of IR structure determination happens inside one narrow decade of it, 4000 to 400 cm⁻¹.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Build as a wide SVG. Center: a horizontal band of six abutting colored rectangles with thin dark dividers and torn/wavy vertical edges at far left and far right; color order left→right deep purple (Ultraviolet), medium violet (Visible, narrow), pale pink (Near infrared), saturated pink (Infrared, widest), very pale pink (Far infrared), pale sage green (Microwaves), each with its name centered in dark text. Directly below, a log wavelength axis labeled 'λ (cm)' at far left with decade ticks 10⁻⁵ … 10⁻¹ evenly spaced; segment boundaries must land at their correct log positions (IR spans 2.5×10⁻⁴ to 2.5×10⁻³ cm). Two thin elbowed leader lines drop from those two IR boundaries to annotation blocks below reading λ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ cm / = 2.5 µm / ṽ = 4000 cm⁻¹ and λ = 2.5 × 10⁻³ cm / = 25 µm / ṽ = 400 cm⁻¹. Above the band a thick leftward arrow with a horizontal gradient from pale yellow at the right tail to deep orange-red at the left head, bold 'Energy' label centered on it. Overlay a draggable vertical marker line (dark, with a round handle on the axis) plus a readout card near the top-right showing λ (cm), λ (µm), ṽ (cm⁻¹), E (kJ/mol) and the current region name, values recomputed live. In the 'Organic IR window' view, dim everything outside the IR segment, stretch the 2.5–25 µm span across the full width, and swap the bottom axis to a decreasing wavenumber scale (4000, 3000, 2000, 1500, 1000, 400 cm⁻¹) to mirror how IR spectra are conventionally plotted.

discrepancies: The Visible band is drawn at true physical width (3.8–7.8 ×10⁻⁵ cm) so it is much narrower than in the source, forcing its 'Visible' label to auto-shrink to a noticeably smaller size than the neighbouring band labels — the source shows a wider Visible box with uniform label size.

Band-label and axis-tick type is smaller relative to the strip than in the source (source labels are large, dominant text inside each block); at inline scale '10⁻⁵'…'10⁻¹' and 'Visible' read as fine print.
The callout blocks (λ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ cm / = 2.5 µm / ν̃ = 4000 cm⁻¹) are set in smaller type and sit closer to the axis than in the source, where they are a prominent second tier of annotation.

Energy arrow proportions differ slightly: the source arrowhead is taller/bolder relative to the shaft and the shaft reaches further right, giving the arrow more visual weight than the generated version.
Region boundary positions differ from the printed figure (e.g. UV/Visible boundary sits near 10⁻⁴.⁴² instead of the source's ~10⁻⁴.⁶), shifting the block widths slightly.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-composed recreation of the IR spectrum strip with torn edges, gradient Energy arrow, correct colours and both printed callouts, backed by genuinely useful interactions (λ slider with live ν̃/E readout, 6-step guided demo, zoom-to-IR-window toggle); main weaknesses are a too-narrow Visible band whose label auto-shrinks and generally smaller label typography than the source's bold hierarchy.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound (scores 5 on concept and interactivity); remaining issues are implementation details—band widths, boundary positions, label typography scale, and callout/arrow proportions—that the generator can fix directly.
